sections.title: CORSI/JI-epro_3000/Class file/workflow_sample XML activities_guidelines.txt
paragraphs: Basic [segreto] steps that use shared folder manual approvers (with explanation):

sections.title: MULTIPLE ELEMENT STATIC WORKFLOW
paragraphs: <Activity name="Dept-Chemistry"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Department" /> <FolderRef name="Chemistry Approvals" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ Owner.Department = "Chemistry" && [Product.Radioactive = true] ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

The workflow activity above is named “Dept-Chemistry” and is a manual activity, which means that someone will need to manually approve this requisition if the rule criteria are true. The step that this activity will happen in is the “Department” step, and the shared folder where approvers will be added is the folder named “Chemistry Approvals” (if this is a new workflow step, or new Workflow Folder, you will need to create a shared folder called Chemistry Approvals and add an approver(s) to it – the user will need to have requisition approval permissions in order to be assigned). The rule uses basic workflow objects to evaluate whether the document owner (requisitioner) has an assigned HR department of “Chemistry”, and also whether there is a product in the requisition with a Product Type of “radioactive”. If the Owner is both in the department Chemistry, AND (denoted by the &&) there is a radioactive item in the requisition, the requisition will route to the explicit folder noted in the FolderRef section, “Chemistry”. If the user is in the Chemistry department and submits a requisition that does not have a radioactive item, the requisition will not stop at this particular activity.

sections.title: APPROVAL BASED ON ITEMS PURCHASED
paragraphs: <Activity name="Green Check"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Green Products" /> <FolderRef name="Purchasing Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ [Product.GreenProduct=true] ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

The workflow activity above is named “Green Check” and is a manual activity, which means that someone will need to manually approve this requisition if the rule criteria are true. The step that this activity will happen in is the “Green Products” step, and the shared folder where approvers will be added is the folder named “Purchasing Approval” (if this is a new workflow step, you will need to create a shared folder called Purchasing Approval and add approvers). The rule uses basic workflow objects to evaluate whether the requisition contains a line item with the Product Type of “Green”. If it does, the requisition will route to the explicit folder called “Purchasing Approval.” If there is not a line item with this product type, the requisition will not stop at this activity for approval.

An Example that Uses an Advanced Dynamic Workflow Rule Evaluation (only new concepts will be explained in detail): <Activity name="Director Approval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Director Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Director Approval") == true ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>MultiElementDynamic</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="RuleGroupInternalName"> <AttrValue lang="default">Director Approval</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>
This rule shows some new concepts:
1. <Rule><![CDATA[ Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Director Approval") == true ]]></Rule>:

This line shows an ADW rule. a. Document. Indicates that this evaluates the entire document. b. RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation shows that an ADW rule is being evaluated. In this case the rule being evaluated is Director Approval. This rule can be found in the Advanced Dynamic Workflow section of workflow configuration. There many rules can be configured under ADW. A document stops here if any one of the ADW rules in the group are true.
2. <Attribute name="RuleGroupInternalName">:

The attribute name line will display in SelectSite and makes it easy to see which ADW rule group is evaluated in this activity. a. <AttrValue lang="default">Director Approval</AttrValue> : This shows the rule group name itself.

sections.title: AUTOMATED STEP THAT REQUIRES MULTIPLE RULE EVALUATIONS
paragraphs: <Activity name="PO Distribution"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="PO Distribution" /> <FolderRef name="Distribute PO" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Manual Purchase Order") in {"true"}) && !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Order Category") in {"2 - Confirming - Do Not Distribute"}) ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>
This activity covers a couple new ideas:
1. <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> : This rule will not require a user to approve the step. This means that the step will complete automatically.

2. <FolderRef name="Distribute PO" /> : This line may look familiar from the previous activities, but since this step is automated it works a little bit differently. Automated activities do not use a Shared Workflow folder like manual activities. Instead, automated activities take advantage of workflow robots. Robots are what allow automated steps to function without user approval. You can see what robot is being used for this folder under the Workflow Folder Import/Export tab in workflow setup.

3. <Rule><![CDATA[ !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Manual Purchase Order") in {"true"}) && !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Order Category") in {"2 - Confirming - Do Not Distribute"}) ]]></Rule>: This rule shows some interesting concepts:

a. !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Manual Purchase Order") in {"true"}) i. This shows that the rule is looking at a Custom Field value at the document level. ii. The rule is looking to see if the value of the Manual Purchase Order Custom Field has a value of true. iii. Notice the ! in front of this rule. If you see ! at the beginning of any rule, then a document will only stop if that rule IS NOT true. In this case, as long as the Manual Purchase Order is not true, the document will stop here. b. && - When you see two "and" symbols like this (&&) that means that the rule following the preceding rule MUST also be true. This allows customers to require several criteria in order for a document to stop. Many && can be used in a given activity.

sections.title: NOTIFICATION MANAGED THROUGH STATIC WORKFLOW:
paragraphs: <Activity name="EH&S Notification"> <ActivityType>notification</ActivityType> <FolderRef name="EH&S Notification" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ [Product.Radioactive = true || Product.RadioactiveMinor = true || Product.HazMat = true || Product.Controlled = true || Product.Toxin = true || Product.SelectAgent = true] ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>
Let's take a look at the rule itself:

1. <Rule><![CDATA[ [Product.Radioactive = true || Product.RadioactiveMinor = true || Product.HazMat = true || Product.Controlled = true || Product.Toxin = true || Product.SelectAgent = true] ]]></Rule>:

a. Notice the || between each rule evaluation; this represents an OR. This means that a document will stop if any one of these rules is true. Unlike the && found in the above example, all of these rules do not have to be true for the rule to be triggered. This allows an activity to be triggered based on separate and distinct criteria. b. The rules in this activity are looking at the products contained in the document. This is indicated by the “Product (dot)” prefix. Each product here contains different product attribute flags. This allows customers to stop documents that contain any product they want that contains any one of these attribute flags.

sections.title: TYPICAL EXAMPLES OF WORKFLOW ACTIVITIES CODE
paragraphs: There are an endless number of approvals clients might want, and numerous options for coding them. Here are some common ePro workflow needs, and samples of code we can examine.

sections.title: ACTIVITYSTART
paragraphs: The first item in the Activity Section looks like this: <!--====== Activities ======--> <Activity name="START"> <ActivityType>start</ActivityType> <Rule /> <FolderSelectionRule>Dummy</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

sections.title: DEPARTMENT APPROVALS
paragraphs: This activity uses Dynamic Workflow. It’s shorter than some because it includes no attributes does not need a FolderRef line. The system checks the “Department” folded to see if an approval is required for the Department on the requester’s profile. An administrator must manage the Dynamic Workflow settings for each Department under Setup > Organization Structure and Settings > Configure Departments. <Activity name="DepartmentApproval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Department Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[Document.RequiresDepartmentalApproval() == true]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>Department</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

Below is an activity that would accommodate Department approvals using ADW instead of Dynamic Workflow. At this point in the process, the system checks a Rule Group called “Department Approval” to see if any rules exist that require the document to stop for review. An administrator must manage the rules and approvers from Setup > Workflow Setup > ___ Workflow Setup > Advanced Dynamic Workflow > Rule Mgmt.

<Activity name="DepartmentApproval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Department Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Department Approval") == true]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>MultiElementDynamic</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="RuleGroupInternalName"> <AttrValue lang="default">Department Approval</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: BUDGET APPROVALS
paragraphs: The example below has a different name but could achieve a similar goal. This activity uses Dynamic Workflow to see if approval is required. Notice the FolderSelectionRule is CustomFieldValue. The system checks the value of a specific custom field named acctElement10 to see if approvers are named or required for that value (Note that “acctElement10” is the “internal name” for that custom field, which is what the XML requires. From the Support Notes below we can deduce that the display name for acctElement10 is “Account Code.”). Notice that in this activity there is also a flag that would allow an approver with sourcing permissions to initiate a sourcing event here. Note that the rule includes a component that says the request would stop ONLY if there is no credit card number – in other words, if the organization is using pCard and this requisition is a credit card purchase, it gets to skip this step. <Activity name="Budget Manager Approval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Budget Manager Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[Document.RequiresCustomFieldValueApproval("acctElement10") == true && [DocLine.CreditCardNumber = ""]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>CustomFieldValue</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>AllowCreateSourcingEvent</Flag> <Attribute name="wfFolderRuleCustomFieldName"> <AttrValue lang="default">acctElement10</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Budget manager approves based on Account Code segment</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Budget manager approves based on Account Code segment.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: DIRECTOR APPROVALS
paragraphs: This activity would accommodate a similar approval in a different way. It uses ADW; rules created and assigned to the “Director Approval” rule group would be evaluated to determine if the request would need to stop. Rules could be created based on a variety of triggers, and with multiple factors if needed. <Activity name="Director Approval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Director Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Director Approval") == true ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>MultiElementDynamic</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="RuleGroupInternalName"> <AttrValue lang="default">Director Approval</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: FINANCIAL APPROVAL
paragraphs: Financial Approvals functionality allows organizations to trigger approvals based on a user’s financial limits. If this type of workflow approval is used by an organization, it is typically the first manual approval step in the workflow process. This means that outside of auto-rejections and other system validations, a user’s financial approver is the first person to review and approve or reject the line items in the requisition. Financial approval can be implemented for requisitions, purchase orders, or invoices. Financial Approval is required when a user submits a requisition, purchase order or invoice that is above their allowed limit, in which case, approval is required by a specified approver. For example, David Jones is assigned the Requester role with a requisition limit of [importo]. He submits a requisition for [importo] which does not require Financial Approval. He submits a second requisition for [importo], and financial approval is required. In order for this to work:
1. “Org Has Financial Approvers” must be enabled. This can be accomplished via Setup > Workflow Setup > General Workflow Settings.

2. Financial limits must be set on the user profile. This can be managed through user roles. It’s possible to set limits for requisition total, line item amount. It’s also possible to set a financial limit for an approver’s approval limit – meaning if the amount is about that, an additional financial approval step will be required.

3. Financial Approvers must be assigned for each user. Some organizations assign approvers to each of its users and others allow their users to determine who can approve their orders. Each user can have one or more financial approver assigned. The Financial Approvers are configured on the user's profile under Default User Settings > Financial Approvers.

This calls for a “static” workflow activity where the rules that would trigger an approval are written into the XML code. In the case below, the rule says an item would stop if the user’s requisition total limit is exceeded, OR if their line-item limit is exceeded. Financial Approval can also be used without reference to spending limits – you could direct ALL requests to Financial Approvers by using an “all” rule instead of the one below. <Activity name="Financial Approval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Financial Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[(Document.Total > Owner.UserLimit("WfLimitPurchasingReqTotal") || [DocLine.Total > Owner.UserLimit("WfLimitPurchasingReqLine")] || ([Document.Total = 0] && Document.Total = Owner.UserLimit("WfLimitPurchasingReqTotal")))]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>UserSelectedApprover</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>FinancialApproval</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">User’s requisition or line item purchasing limit exceeded</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

The FolderSelectionRule seen above is one we haven’t seen previously. UserSelectedApprover tells the system to check the approver selected by the user for this request. Some organizations let users choose from a short list of approvers, but others have administrators specify the approver for each user.

sections.title: “REPORTS TO" APPROVALS
paragraphs: Financial Approvers functionality works well when multiple approvers might be able to approve requests . If the organization wants one specific person named as the approver, they can use the “Reports To” functionality.

When “Reports To” is enabled, each user can have a specific person they ‘report to’ who always looks at their purchases. Usually this would be their supervisor, but in some cases it might be someone who doesn’t actually supervise the requester, but is supposed to review every requisition from their department (for instance).

The code for a Reports To activity in workflow can be set up like the code for Financial Approvers, also using UserSelectedApprover in the FolderSelectionRule tag. The example below uses ADW to tell the system to check a rule group called “Indirect Requisition” to see if the request needs to be approved. But if it does, the system will figure out who should approve it by looking at the user’s profile and checking who they Report To.

<Activity name="Manager Approval"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Manager Approval" /> <Rule><![CDATA[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Indirect Requisition") == true]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>UserSelectedApprover</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

sections.title: EH&S APPROVAL
paragraphs: Next, let’s look at an example that uses an Advanced Dynamic Workflow rule evaluation to trigger a notification, not an approval. If the item is radioactive, radioactive minor, controlled, toxin or select agent, a system notification will be sent to any approver named on the Shared Folder called “EH&S Notification.” <Activity name="EH&S Notification"> <ActivityType>notification</ActivityType> <FolderRef name="EH&S Notification" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ [Product.Radioactive = true || Product.RadioactiveMinor = true || Product.HazMat = true || Product.Controlled = true || Product.Toxin = true || Product.SelectAgent = true] ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

sections.title: MISSING SUPPLIER CATCH
paragraphs: The rule in this activity says if the Supplier ID is blank, the request must be directed to someone who can correct that. Who gets it is managed via a Shared Folder called Missing Supplier Catch. <Activity name="Missing Supplier Catch"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Missing Supplier Catch" /> <FolderRef name="Missing Supplier Catch" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Supplier.ID == ""]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>AllowCreateSourcingEvent</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">No supplier is specified. An approver must select one before advancing.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: MISSING APPROVER CATCH
paragraphs: This activity uses ADW. <Activity name="Missing Approver Catch"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Missing Approver Catch" /> <FolderRef name="Missing Approver Catch" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresCustomFieldValueApproval("acctElement10") == false ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>AllowCreateSourcingEvent</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">If an Account Code approver is not namaed, an admin must add approver.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: MIXED ORDER AUTO-RETURN
paragraphs: This automated activity checks the cart for items that should not be together, and returns the requisition to the requester with the message seen in the “wfActivitySupportNote” explaining they can’t submit a cart/requisition that includes items that need POs with items that do not. The FormType names listed within the rule seen below are specific to the organization, so the rule would need to be re-written for other clients. <Activity name="Mixed Order Auto-Return"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Mixed Order Auto-Return" /> <FolderRef name="Auto-Return" /> <Rule><![CDATA[([Product.FormType ~ "/NonPO/"] && [Product.FormType !~ "/NonPO/"]) || ([Product.FormType ~ "/NoDistro/"] && [Product.FormType !~ "/NoDistro/"]) || ([Product.FormType ~ "/AutoInv/"] && [Product.FormType !~ "/AutoInv/"])]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>AllowCreateSourcingEvent</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Items that do not create POs cannot be mixed with items that do create POs. Items that do not distribute to supplier cannot be mixed with items that distribute to suppliers. Items that auto-invoice cannot be mixed with items that do not auto-invoice. This is managed by use of Form Type internal name.</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Items that do not create POs cannot be mixed with itmes that do create POs.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

pCARD LIMIT CHECK This automated activity checks to see if the requisition includes a credit card number, and if so, if the total surpasses the user’s pCard limit. If both those things are true, the requisition goes to an internal folder called “Auto-Reject” which runs a robot (named in the “Workflow Folders” XML file) which rejects the requisition and tells the user it’s because they exceeded their pCard limit. <Activity name="pCard Limit Check"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="pCard Limit Check" /> <FolderRef name="Auto-Reject" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[DocLine.CreditCardNumber != ""] && Document.Total >= Owner.UserLimit("WfLimitLpoReqLine")]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Your requisition has been rejected because you exceeded your pCard limit.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: FISCAL YEAR END HOLD
paragraphs: Sometimes organizations take their ERPs offline to process data at the fiscal year’s end. <Activity name="InitialFiscalYearEnd"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Initial Fiscal Year End" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Fiscal Year End Hold") == true]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>MultiElementDynamic</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="RuleGroupInternalName"> <AttrValue lang="default">Initial Fiscal Year End Hold</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Stops requisitions to hold while ERP is down for processing Fiscal Year End</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Help for Initial Fiscal Year End Hold</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: PR VALIDATION
paragraphs: Next, we have code that would facilitate a PR validation where the system checks in the ERP to see if there is enough money available in the appropriate budget codes. This requires a PR Validation integration. In this case, some requisitions could skip this step because there is an “Omit from” Rule Group where administrators could set up rules that would allow some requests to go through without needing validation. If the requisition doesn’t meet that criteria, the system performs a budget check by sending a notification to the ERP and awaiting a response that confirms there’s enough money. It’s typical for organizations that use PR Validation to include it twice in requisition workflow – an ‘initial’ check in the beginning and a ‘final’ check later. Note that the “wait” activity includes a flag that does not allow items to bypass this step by being expedited. If there isn’t enough money, the requisition is returned to the requester. <Activity name="InitialPRValidation"> <ActivityType>notification</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Initial PR Validation" /> <FolderRef name="WaitForPRApprovals" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Omit from PR Validation") == false]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Validates the PR against the ERP</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Help for PR Validation</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

<Activity name="InitialPRValidationWait"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Initial PR Validation" /> <FolderRef name="WaitForPRApprovals" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Omit from PR Validation") == false]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>NoBypass</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Holds PR while waiting for asynchronous response from the ERP.</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">Help for PR Validation Wait</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfReturnReqInsteadOfReject"> <AttrValue lang="default">true</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

Note that BOTH of these activities occur during the Initial PR Validation step. The Activity Relationships might be set up as follows, indicating that after the Initial Fiscal Year End, there are two concurrent activities in the next step. <ActivityRelationship previous="Return2" next="InitialFiscalYearEnd" /> <ActivityRelationship previous="InitialFiscalYearEnd" next="InitialPRValidation" /> <ActivityRelationship previous="InitialFiscalYearEnd" next="InitialPRValidationWait" /> <ActivityRelationship previous="InitialPRValidation" next="Approval-1" /> <ActivityRelationship previous="InitialPRValidationWait" next="Approval-1" /> <ActivityRelationship previous="Approval-1" next="Approval-2" />

sections.title: INVALID OR MISSING DISTRIBUTION
paragraphs: Next is Static workflow activity which stops requests with no valid distribution address for an order. <Activity name="Missing Distribution"> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Missing Distribution" /> <FolderRef name="Missing Distribution" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ Document.HasInvalidDistribution() == true ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

sections.title: CREATE PO
paragraphs: The next activity is an automated one. At this point the requisition goes to an internal folder called “Create PO” that specifies the system should create a PO. It does NOT do that if a “NonPO” form type was used. <Activity name="Create PO"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Create PO" /> <FolderRef name="Create PO" /> <Rule><![CDATA[![Product.FormType ~ "/NonPO/"]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>NoBypass</Flag> <Attribute name="wfActivitySupportNote"> <AttrValue lang="default">Do not create a PO for internal forms (formtype starts with I)</AttrValue> </Attribute> <Attribute name="wfActivityHelp"> <AttrValue lang="default">This is a system step that creates a JAGGAER PO.</AttrValue> </Attribute> </Activity>

sections.title: PO DISTRIBUTION
paragraphs: Next is another automated activity that would occur during Purchase Order workflow. This rule hinges on the values of a couple of custom fields that the organization has created and placed on the PO Document. <Activity name="PO Distribution"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="PO Distribution" /> <FolderRef name="Distribute PO" /> <Rule><![CDATA[ !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Manual Purchase Order") in {"true"}) && !(Document.CustomFieldValues("Order Category") in {"2 - Confirming - Do Not Distribute"}) ]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>

sections.title: AUTO INVOICE
paragraphs: The following activity for PO workflow checks a rule group called Auto Invoice to see if the system should automatically generate an invoice from the PO. The rule group might have a rule that specifies invoices are automatically created for orders from certain suppliers with whom the client has set up this arrangement for faster payment. Other criteria could also be used. Any PO that meets the criteria of a rule in Auto Invoice would be sent to an internal (explicit) folder called Create Invoice, which would run a robot that would create an invoice.

<Activity name="Auto Invoice"> <ActivityType>automated</ActivityType> <StepRef name="Auto Invoice" /> <FolderRef name="Create Invoice" /> <Rule><![CDATA[[Document.RequiresRuleGroupEvaluation("Auto Invoice") == true]]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> </Activity>
